q: Why does an LRU cache need a DOUBLY linked list?
options: To remove a node from the middle in O(1), you need its previous node
why: The map gives you the node; unlinking it needs prev as well as next.

q: In an LRU cache, what does a successful get(key) do besides returning the value?
options: Moves the key to the most-recently-used end
why: Reading counts as using it, so it's no longer the least recent.

q: Add Two Numbers: l1 = [9, 9], l2 = [1] (i.e. 99 + 1). What's the result list?
why: Digits are stored in reverse: 100 → [0, 0, 1]. The final carry needs its own node.

q: Reorder List (L0 → Ln → L1 → Ln−1 …) in O(1) space. Which steps?
options: Find the middle, reverse the second half, interleave the two halves
why: Three standard moves, each O(n), none needing extra space.

q: Reversing nodes between positions left and right takes…
options: O(right − left) time after reaching left, O(1) space
why: Walk to the node before left, then right − left O(1) moves.

q: Copy List with Random Pointer: why two passes with a map?
options: A random pointer may point to a node whose copy doesn't exist yet
why: Create every copy first (old → new), then set next and random through the map.
